results.corrected_extracted: eFigure 5 plots, for each group, the adjusted mean daily probability of a self-reported nonfatal overdose across the 28-day observation period against age, on a log scale; the article's Results say the association was modified by age in adjusted but not in unadjusted analyses, and give no age-specific ratios. Editors' reading of the figure (measured from the image): the probabilities are drawn with 95% bands over ages 19 to 76; the strip group's line falls steeply with age while the comparison group's stays nearly flat, the two crossing at about age 42, so the modelled risk is higher in the strip group among younger and lower among older participants; the two bands overlap at every age; the plotted probabilities (about 0.0003 to 0.014 in the strip group and 0.002 to 0.003 in the comparison group) are well below the mean daily risk of 0.02 in the article's Results, so they were computed at covariate values the figure does not state.
results.note: Figure reading reproduced (lines 0.014 to 0.0003 and 0.0035 to 0.0024, crossing at age 41.7, bands overlapping throughout). But 0.02 is not in Table 3 (estimates of association only): it is in the Results paragraph and Abstract.

cards.your_judgment: Item 7: no. Item 8: no. Overall confidence stays critically low.
cards.note: Item 7: Figure 1 (AM p. 13) gives only a count with one reason (50 full texts without original strip data); neither the manuscript nor the four supplementary files list excluded studies, so not even partial yes. Item 8: Table 1 describes the 91 in aggregate; per-study detail covers subsets only (13 programmes in Table 3; 14, 7 and 7 studies in Supplemental Tables 1-3), never population, intervention, comparator, outcomes and design for each study, so partial yes is not met. Critically low holds regardless: the Methods describe no appraisal, so critical items 9 and 13 alone are two critical flaws (item 4 a third, per the card). Minor: the item 8 note's 'setting, year, a population note and the figure used' fits Supplemental Table 1 only; Table 2 gives place, year, number and result, Table 3 place and percentage.

cards.item: ROBINS-I, bias in classification of interventions
cards.note: All but one fact in the note is in Appendix A, the paper or the corrigendum: dates, five departures, reasons and their dates (2023, 2025), 'reasonable researchers' sentence, 12 undiscussed treated jurisdictions, no source-date results, original wording (corrigendum Changes 2-3), 'Reforms enacted' heading, 'Months Relative to Enactment' axes, silence on the six undated states and on mid-month dates. Error: 'a law school's summary' should be the UNC School of Government's summary (not a law school; the card's own key finding says so). '19 jurisdictions' rests on the stated assumption about the six undated states. One in six recomputed: 68 to 79 of 430 to 441 source-implied post-law state-months (15.8% to 17.9%) against 362 coded. My judgment: serious, because the coding of 5 of 19 jurisdictions is post hoc judgment, partly on post-period evidence, published after the results, with no analysis using the source's dates; not critical, because it is documented and the other dates follow the statutes.
